# Pilot Logbook

> Pilot Logbook (pilotlogbook.ca) is a digital pilot logbook app that lets pilots photograph their paper logbook and have AI fill in every flight, then automatically tracks flight hours, currency/recency, duty limits, and aviation-document expiries. It runs on the web and as native iPhone and iPad apps, works offline, and syncs across devices. Built around Canadian aviation regulations (CARs / Transport Canada), with reference-only currency and duty gauges.

## What it does

- AI logbook scanning: photograph a paper logbook page and AI extracts dates, aircraft type, registration, routes, hours, and crew into reviewable flight rows (nothing is auto-saved — the pilot confirms).
- Currency & recency tracking: day/night passenger recency, IFR (6 approaches / 6 months), and custom rules, over calendar-month windows.
- Duty & rest tracking: 703 / 704 / 705 flight-time, flight-duty-period, and rest limits.
- Aviation document tracking: medicals, ratings, and recurrent training with Transport Canada expiry math and reminders.
- Import/export: CSV import and export, plus Transport Canada-style PDF logbook and summary export.
- Offline-first with cloud sync; data is encrypted and scoped to each account.

## Pricing

- Free — $0 forever. Unlimited manual logging, flight totals & reports, basic currency tracking, aircraft database, route map, basic PDF export.
- Pro — $10/month (or $8.33/month billed annually — 2 months free). Adds AI logbook scanning, document OCR, unlimited multi-device cloud sync, advanced currency & expiry alerts, professional PDF export, backup & restore, and native iPhone/iPad/Mac apps.
- Professional — $15/month (or $12.50/month billed annually — 2 months free). Adds unlimited AI scanning, airline roster import, company reports, advanced analytics, duty & rest analysis, and priority support.
- 14-day free trial on Pro and Professional; scan your first 10 pages free; no credit card required to start; cancel anytime. Prices in CAD.

## Notes

- Audience: student, private, commercial, and airline pilots — with a focus on Canada (CARs / Transport Canada).
- Currency and duty figures are a reference aid; the CARs and a pilot's company minima always govern.
